overview.summary: The canary_hpc extension batches Canary jobs and submits batches to HPC schedulers through hpc_connect.

layouts.flat: Jobs within a batch do not depend on each other. Batches may depend on other batches.
layouts.atomic: Dependency-connected components are kept together. Batches do not depend on other batches.

node_policies.same: All jobs in a partition require the same node count.
node_policies.any: Jobs with different node counts may be batched together.

targets.duration: Create batches targeting approximate simulated runtime.
targets.count=max: Create the maximum number of batches allowed by the selected layout.

workspace_layout.note: Batch directories are session-scoped artifacts under .canary/sessions/, not under .canary/cache/.

execution.summary: HPC batches are submitted through hpc_connect. Each batch receives a generated resource pool and then launches Canary inside the allocation.

timeouts.queue_timeout: Maximum time waiting for scheduler start.
timeouts.run_timeout: Estimated batch runtime multiplied by timeout multiplier.

commands.batch_log: canary hpc log <BATCH_ID>  -- print the stdout log for a batch
commands.query_batches: canary query batch <BATCH_ID>  -- inspect a batch.lock (requires canary_query_subcommand hook)
commands.query_all_batches: canary query batches  -- list all batches in the latest session

resource_model.summary: The conductor uses backend node resource counts to generate a topology-aware resource pool for each batch.
resource_model.multi_node: Batches may request multiple scheduler nodes when jobs require multiple Canary nodes.

debug_logging.summary: Run with --debug or -v -v to enable DEBUG-level logging captured in .canary/logs/canary.0.log.
logged_at_debug: Per-batch workspace directory, job count, and dependency count at creation
Batch packing summary: algorithm, total batches, total jobs
Per-batch packing row: id, jobs, nodes, estimated runtime
Batch submission: id, estimated runtime, dependency count
Batch completion: id, rc, pass/fail counts, total wall time, queue wait, running time
Stale cache cap firings: which jobs had their cached mean clamped to declared timeout
